deathSays.line: You wake up with dirt in your mouth and blood on your hands that isn't yours. The sky is the wrong color — not sunset-wrong, wound-wrong. Avery Tan. Farmer. From Columbus, Ohio. That was yesterday. This is now. You have: Dead Phone, Contract Quill, Knife roll, Coat button, Trail compass. That's everything you own in this world. Haven. Twelve people. The fire is lit. Last night, something walked past the treeline on two legs. Too tall. It stopped. It listened. Then it kept going. Nobody slept after that.
Movement — a waddling opossum, playing dead (badly).
👁 You know this one's trick: it plays dead. Don't fall for it — or do, and be ready when it wakes.

One mouse is a snack. Fifty mice is a meal. Do the math. It's dead. The carcass is there on the ground — search the body if you want the meat. But you don't know this flesh. Clean it, test it cautiously, or ask someone who knows. And don't leave it long: meat rots where it lies.
